name: Elasah
overview: Elasah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically as the son of Pashhur who had married a foreign wife. This detail highlights a significant issue addressed in the biblical text where intermarriage with foreign women was a matter of concern for the community. Beyond this, Scripture provides no additional personal notes about Elasah.
namesAndTitles: The name Elasah means 'G-d has fashioned,' reflecting a Hebrew theophoric element that acknowledges God's creative work. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 10:22, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine craftsmanship.
familyAndRelationships: Elasah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Pashhur, establishing a direct father-son relationship as recorded in Ezra 10:22. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Elasah's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his identification as a son of Pashhur, who was involved in the issue of intermarriage with foreign women among the Levites. This association places Elasah within the context of the post-exilic community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands. His mention underscores the challenges faced by the returned exiles in upholding God's standards amid cultural and social pressures.
